title: Determine the Winner of a Bowling Game
summary: Given two arrays, player1 and player2, representing the number of pins hit by each player in a bowling game where each turn involves hitting exactly 10 pins over n turns, calculate the score for each player.
statement: Given two arrays, player1 and player2, representing the number of pins hit by each player in a bowling game where each turn involves hitting exactly 10 pins over n turns, calculate the score for each player. The score of a turn is defined as 2xi if the player hit 10 pins in either the previous or the second previous turn, and xi otherwise. Return 1 if player1 has a higher score, 2 if player2 has a higher score, and 0 if the scores are equal.
constraints: Both arrays give pins knocked down on equal numbers of turns.
A turn scores double when either of the preceding two turns for that player knocked down ten pins.
Return 1 for a higher player-one score, 2 for player two, or 0 for a tie.
hints: For turn i, inspect indices i-1 and i-2 only when they exist.
Double the current pins if either inspected value is ten, then compare totals.
The loop applies the rule to every turn exactly once; the final three-way comparison directly implements the required winner code.
editorial: The loop applies the rule to every turn exactly once; the final three-way comparison directly implements the required winner code.

tests.explanation: Player one receives doubled scores after the ten-pin turn and wins.
Player two receives the larger bonus-adjusted total and wins.
